title: ECP5 (non-ULX3S) gateware survey on GitHub
description: Gateware for other ECP5 boards (OrangeCrab, LUNA, iCESugar-Pro, HAD2019, Colorlight, ButterStick, ECPIX-5…): 114 repos, 24 recommended.

blocks.text:
Survey date: 2026-09-27. Research only: nothing cloned. Scope: Lattice ECP5 boards other than
ULX3S / ULX4M / ULX5M (those are in `docs/github-survey.md`); iCE40, Gowin and Xilinx-only repos excluded.
702 unique repos came back from 53 searches. After removing forks, empty repos, off-topic matches
and ULX*/iCE40/Gowin/Xilinx hits, **114 repos** are listed below.

items:
`verified (...)`: the full recursive file list was read at the shown commit. It contains a
`.lpf` constraint file (or the `.pcf`-named LPF used by OrangeCrab/ButterStick) and HDL sources.
When a Makefile was found, its build commands were read for `yosys` / `nextpnr-ecp5` / `ecppack`.

`partial`: Python/Amaranth/LiteX sources were seen but no `.lpf` file. Pins come from a framework
board file, so this is normal for LiteX and Amaranth.
`unverified`: name or README only, or the file list shows no constraints or HDL.

Toolchain `open` means the Makefile, build.sh or README calls yosys + nextpnr-ecp5 + ecppack.
`(README flow)` means the README states it but no Makefile was found.

blocks.text: **Status 2026-09-28:** all 24 are cloned and in the [catalogue](catalogue.md). Items 1–14 on 2026-09-27 (items 2 and 11 were already there from the ULX3S survey), item 21 (joshajohnson/ecp5-mini-projects) on request with kbeckmann/pergola_projects (its upstream), items 15–20 and 22–24 on 2026-09-28.
Priority goes to plain Verilog, the open toolchain, reusable cores and good board examples.

items:
**Spritetm/hadbadge2019_fpgasoc**: the largest open-flow ECP5 SoC seen. Dual PicoRV32, LCD/video,
audio synth, PSRAM (QSPI) controller and USB, with 27 Makefiles. The blocks can be reused on ULX3S.
**wuxx/Colorlight-FPGA-Projects**: vendor examples for 5A-75B, i5 and i9 (13 lpf). The most popular cheap ECP5 boards.
**wuxx/icesugar-pro**: vendor examples for iCESugar-Pro (HDMI, SDRAM, blink).
**orangecrab-fpga/orangecrab-examples**: official OrangeCrab examples in Verilog, including USB-ACM.
**ultraembedded/orangecrab**: standalone Verilog DDR3 AXI controller + DFI PHY for ECP5 (reusable).
**ultraembedded/ecpix-5**: ultraembedded RISC-V AXI4 SoC + DVI framebuffer (IT6613) on ECPIX-5, all Verilog.
**fdarling/orangecrab-usb-cdc-demo**: small pure-Verilog USB CDC-ACM core (reusable without LiteX).
**gregdavill/luna-usb-serial-acm**: LUNA USB-ACM exported as one Verilog module (reusable anywhere).
**mangelajo/orangecrab-usb**: Verilog USB device examples (FPGA-USB-Device).
**tallenintegsys/hdmi-orangecrab**: HDMI IP port for ECP5 in SystemVerilog.
**danodus/ecp5_hdmi_audio_video**: ECP5 HDMI transmitter with audio, active 2026.
**sefbkn/versa-ecp5-demo**: open-flow Gigabit Ethernet with RGMII + SGMII (rare SGMII on nextpnr).
**tomverbeure/ecp5_jtag**: JTAGG user-logic access, a reusable debug block.
**cheyao/icepi-zero**: 24 open-flow gateware examples for a popular new ECP5 board (827 stars, active).
**hexagon5un/hackaday_supercon_2019_logic_noise_FPGA_workshop**: Verilog audio/synth building blocks.
**emeb/orangecrab_adc**: ADC/audio SDR gateware on the open flow.
**mebner86/icesugar-pro_sound2fft**: I2S → FFT → HDMI in a step-by-step series (17 projects, 2026).
**DatanoiseTV/colorlight-i9-aes67**: AES67 audio-over-Ethernet on i9 (37 Verilog files, 2026).
**lucysrausch/colorlight-led-cube**: HUB75 LED driver + LiteEth core on 5A-75B (112 stars).
**kholia/Colorlight-5A-75B**: DDS/SSB radio + Docker open-flow recipes.
**joshajohnson/ecp5-mini-projects**: 40 Verilog files of open-flow examples.
**xtrinch/fpga-bitcoin-miner**: pipelined SHA-256 on ECP5-EVN (reusable hash core).

**greatscottgadgets/luna**: the reference USB framework (Amaranth). Ranked lower because it is not plain
Verilog, but it is the only complete open USB 2.0/3.0 gateware stack for ECP5.
**racerxdl/colorlight-picorv32**: minimal PicoRV32 SoC + HUB75 on Colorlight i5.

items:
No rate-limit errors (HTTP 403) on search. The core API was hardly used. File lists came from github.com's
`tree/HEAD` + `tree-list/<oid>` JSON endpoints, which do not count against the 60/h API budget.
Makefiles and READMEs came from raw.githubusercontent.com.

Only the first 3 Makefiles of each repo were read for toolchain calls. A repo that builds from a
script with another name shows no toolchain and is marked from its README.

Code search (`extension:lpf`) was not used because it needs authentication. Repos whose name,
description and README never mention the board are therefore missed.

Forks that carry their own work were dropped along with trivial forks. Examples are the many
CFU-Playground and microwatt forks, and gregdavill/foboot.

Dropped as out of scope: lawrie/tinyfpga_examples (TinyFPGA BX, iCE40 `.pcf`),
gmejiamtz/ecp5-project-template (ULX3S target), and any ULX3S/ULX4M/ULX5M(-GS) repos.
